chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: After the Navy: Downbeat with Lee Young; choosing Heywood over Hampton
summary: Royal turned from Hampton's marching format to Eddie Heywood after a Sunny Side of the Street recording.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And Eddie Haywood, you worked with (inaudible)?

Eddie Haywood, I worked with him. That was my -- when I first got out of service, the ending of 1945, I came back in town and I worked for about a week with a little band down at the Downbeat down on Central Avenue, with Lee Young's orchestra. It was a good little swing thing down there. We had three horns and a rhythm section and we worked in a little joint called the Downbeat. Kay Star's (PHONETIC) husband owned

Right, Hal Stanley owned it. Then, after about a week, Eddie Haywood called me up -- no, Lionel Hampton came in town and wanted me to reenter his band. So he set up a deal wherein I was supposed to meet him and after really thinking about it, I wasn't just sure whether I actually wanted to go back with Lionel Hampton or not, because he had incorporated so much marching into his band that that really didn't interest me because I was more musical-minded and I didn't dig walking through the aisles, parading, with "Flying Home." So I was sort of in between thoughts and while he was waiting for me to come to rehearsal, Eddie Haywood called me up and asked me to come to a recording session.

When I did, I went out that evening and we made a recording and I played on his record, "The Sunny Side of the Street," with Eddie Haywood and so he immediately wanted to hire me. So, he did on the spot and I didn't go back to Lionel Hampton anymore to do any marching --

-- and I never had much of a desire to ever go back to Lionel Hampton again, because I didn't like his format of playing and I didn't appreciate what he had -- how he had prostituted his band to make an extra buck.
He figures drums weren't for jumping on?
